# Independent audit of the thin-edge all-active-menu obstruction

Audited `candidate e52160c774656005`, Sections 1--9, including its two quantitative facet dependencies. **PASS.** This is an obstruction to a universal individual-source Gamma efficiency assertion, not an OC counterexample or a certificate at a below-OC body minimum.

The actual three fibers are preserved by their convex hull. The endpoint mass is exactly 4 delta^3-3 delta^4, from the Beta(3,2) coordinate-sum density. Endpoint isolation and the middle own-volume lower bound place every deepest source in the middle fiber; the ordinary simplex normal gap places every active continuous direction in one of the five stated cones. The positive-width own core gives the required actual normal derivatives and uniqueness, using the cited attained smoothing theorem.

For a non-edge cone, zero base tilt makes both endpoints identically missed. In an edge cone, pairing an endpoint point with the coordinate-swapped point at the other endpoint cancels every base tilt and leaves a uniformly positive sum of physical margins. Thus the paired captures sum to at least one, and strictly exceed one on any positive-volume transition strip. Finite saturation attains exactly one endpoint volume. Therefore every active cap has the asserted exact outside mass and zero outside coarea, for every base tilt. The endpoint boundary profile bound also follows: continuity of the positive-width capture function extends a zero-volume integral to zero capture everywhere on that compact full-dimensional endpoint body.

At fixed delta, the limiting proper own sections are individually centered at the limiting source. Their vertex-cap intercepts and the permutation symmetries give exactly the two source coordinates and the scalar equation in Section 5. The derivative at the uniform point is 256/75. The unique response dependence is theta_i=(r_i/q_i)/B, and compactness upgrades its limiting uniqueness to uniform convergence over all active menus, including menus with several caps in one cone.

The disputed facet affine-moment calculation in Section 5 is correct. A source facet F_i has dimension three. Its cap at vertex j has FOUR vertices: v_j itself and the three edge-intersection points. Thus the cap VOLUME centroid has coordinate y_k for k distinct from i,j and coordinate y_i+y_j at j. The factor d/(d-1) would instead describe the lower-dimensional CUT section, which is not the measure integrated here. The weighted facet mass is exactly 1/B, and each nonzero barycentric first moment is exactly

    y_k/B+r_k/(4B)=1/(4B).

Consequently all affine moments vanish against W_delta-beta_delta, with no O(alpha) error. The O(alpha^2) error in beta_delta-Gamma follows from the smooth symmetric rational formula and its vanishing first derivative at uniform barycentrics.

The quantitative facet dependency has c_4=(1-4^(-3))/(9*5)=7/320, so Gamma_4 c_4=28/3125 as used. Its proof applies to every nonnegative convex function vanishing at the facet centroid. The weighted strip dependency gives 8(d+1)=40 for d=4, again uniformly over the complete convex cone. Therefore the small cap/weight perturbations preserve a fixed half-gap, including for concentrating sequences of convex tests.

The supporting affine function at the facet centroid has nonnegative mean. Its maximum vertex coefficient controls all negative coefficients, and the indicated corner simplex proves sup|ell|<=3072 integral(phi). This makes the affine L1-profile error uniform relative to the test integral. The decomposition phi=ell+f then gives precisely the source-facet inequality (13).

The tiny simplex E_i lies in the shared patch, has relative volume delta^3/64, and every facet barycentric coordinate is at least delta/16. Both branches of the affine-observability proof check. In the negative-coefficient branch, its corner contributes eta^4/[16(M+eta)^3], which is at least eta^4/[1024(1+eta)^3]. At eta>=delta/8 and delta<=1 this exceeds 2^(-23) delta^4. Thus the stated weaker constant is valid. The conversion to the nonnegative convex test gives epsilon+J_i>=2^(-24)delta^4 I, including zero affine mean.

Finally, physical convexity at each shared facet normal forces the two endpoint traces to pay twice the middle trace on that patch. Half of the strict endpoint profile gap pays the patch observation, and half remains as an endpoint-volume deficit. Since kappa<g_0, the delta^4 observation outweighs the O(alpha^2)=O(delta^6) affine-neutral source excess after delta is fixed sufficiently small; the subsequent width choice controls the uniform profile error. The final strict bound holds for all normal-dependent nonnegative finite convex fields and all actual balanced active menus.

No arbitrary boundary-selector identification, favorable-menu restriction, compactness of normalized convex test functions, or unproved mixed-integer inequality enters this certificate. The heavy middle fiber is essential to its stated scope: the configuration is far above the OC depth threshold.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
